what_happened: Research found that tests/run-all.sh already ships a complete, working --fail-on-new flag plus a committed known-failures.txt manifest (EXPECTED/NEW classification, annotated roster, annotated tally line) -- the exact producer-side mechanism the task description asks to be built. Gate 8 simply never passed --fail-on-new. Further, verify-deploy.sh already has a warn_advisory() primitive (WARN-FINDING channel, excluded from deploy_findings_snapshot's grep '^FINDING ' filter) that is the exact non-blocking-but-visible mechanism needed, with zero required changes to deploy-baseline-lib.sh. This substantially narrows task 445's implementation scope to gate8_run()'s branching logic alone.

Planning dispatch observed that concurrent sibling task 418 (implement phase, same /orchestrate cycle) declares agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/verify-deploy.sh AND __WHOLE_TREE__ in its file_scope -- the same primary edit target this plan's Phase 1 and Phase 5 need. No edit was attempted during planning, so no collision occurred yet, but the implement dispatch for this plan must re-read verify-deploy.sh immediately before editing and stage only its own hunks. Recorded so the implementer does not rediscover the overlap cold.

Planning confirmed a second pre-existing primitive beyond the research finding: verify-deploy.sh's warn_advisory() already writes WARN-FINDING (not FINDING), and deploy_findings_snapshot filters strictly on grep '^FINDING ', so the dispatch's pre/post baseline-skew worry is answered with zero change to lib/deploy-baseline-lib.sh. Additionally confirmed warn_advisory still appends to GATE_DIRTY_LIST, so the --skip-unchanged gate cache (gate 8 is in CACHEABLE_GATES) cannot cache a warm PASS over an all-expected failing corpus -- a hazard a plain pass() design would have introduced.

The convergence guard in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh (condition: probed_dispatch empty AND eligible_tasks non-empty, threshold 3 consecutive cycles) cannot fire when a cycle's zero-dispatch outcome is produced by the self-modification tie-breaker or the __WHOLE_TREE__ ordering deferral, because both gates are applied DOWNSTREAM of the guard. probed_dispatch was non-empty (stderr: 'Contended-path manifest: 83 path(s) contended across 2 dispatched task(s) this cycle') so the guard's else branch reset consecutive_no_dispatch_cycles to 0 on every cycle, while dispatch[] emitted empty. Observed across two identical cycles in this batch: #431 deferred for a __WHOLE_TREE__ collision with out-of-batch non-terminal #409, #445 deferred by the self-modification tie-breaker in favor of #418, and #418/#435 both locked by a concurrent live session -- a configuration in which the loop spins indefinitely with no stop verdict. The orchestrator had to be terminated by operator judgment rather than by the engine's own guard. Remedy direction: evaluate the guard after the admission/deferral gates, or make it compare the emitted dispatch[] length rather than probed_dispatch.

CORRECTION to earlier entry iss_1793992157216_ZCSwKL, which misattributed the mechanism. That entry claimed the self-modification tie-breaker and file-scope-collision deferrals are applied DOWNSTREAM of the convergence guard. Independent verification against the live script shows the opposite: the admission defer at orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh:2084 ('if [ "${admit_decision[$t]:-admit}" = "defer" ]; then ... continue; fi') fires BEFORE probed_dispatch is built at line 2124, so deferred candidates correctly leave probed_dispatch empty and WOULD increment the counter. __WHOLE_TREE__ does not appear in this script at all; it lives in scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh. The actual blind spot is narrower: probed_dispatch is populated from the read-only 'task-lock.sh check' probe, while the real acquire happens later in the live per-task loop whose sole out_dispatch_rows append site is at line 2880. Six exclusion paths sit between the guard and that emission, all invisible to it -- unresolvable project_name, LOCKED BY ANOTHER SESSION AT ACQUIRE TIME, acquire error, orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh failure, identity-seq mismatch, and the identical-dispatch halt. This explains the observed evidence precisely: the two tasks that passed check and failed acquire left probed_dispatch at 2 (matching the '83 path(s) contended across 2 dispatched task(s)' manifest), so the guard saw non-empty and reset to 0 while dispatch[] emitted empty. The guard's own stop_message is self-contradicting: it names the tie-breaker class it does cover and misses the acquire class that actually stalls runs. The durable remediation record is the task directory specs/514_convergence_guard_blind_to_zero_dispatch_cycles/.
